Unlike ray-based approaches such as Local AO, it uses vector quantization clustering to store these distributions in a 2D texture table, allowing real-time updates via GPU texture blending with only two additional texture lookups compared to standard gradient-based shading [S1].

The claim is fully supported by Source [S1]. The source explicitly states that unlike ray-based approaches (e.g., Local AO), the method uses precomputed histograms and clustering (vector quantization) to store intensity distributions in a 2D texture table. It further confirms that this allows real-time updates via GPU texture blending and requires only two additional texture lookups compared to standard gradient-based shading.
